Q: Thank you for taking the time to give this recorded statement. Please state your full name for the record.
A: I'd rather just be referred to by my role in this, if that's alright. I was the passenger.
Q: That's fine. Can you tell me where you were when the collision happened?
A: We were stopped at a light on a main road in Pasadena, Texas, heading east. It was late afternoon and traffic was
fairly heavy.
Q: And what happened next?
A: The driver behind us didn't stop in time. I felt a hard jolt from behind, and my knee hit the dashboard. My head
snapped back too, but the knee is what hurt right away.
Q: Did you get out of the vehicle at the scene?
A: I got out, but I was limping and needed help standing. A bystander held my arm whlie we waited for the police.
Q: Did you seek medical attention that day?
A: Yes, an ambulance took me to the emergency room. They took X-rays and told me there was no break, but the
swelling was bad and they wrapped it.
Q: Have you been seeing a doctor since?
A: Yes, I've had two follow-up visits with an orthopedic clinic. They mentioned possible ligament damage and want an
MRI.
Q: How is the knee affecting your daily life?
A: I can't climb stairs without pain, and I've had to take time off work because standing for long periods is hard.
Sleeping is rough too beacuse I can't find a comfortable position.
Q: Is there anything else you'd like to add to your statement?
A: Only that I'm still waiting on the MRI results, and I'll share those with you once I have them.
Q: Thank you. This concludes the statement.
A: Thank you.
</page>
